unsupported: Established in 1997, the site serves as Samsung Electronics' primary U.S. semiconductor manufacturing base.
The fab is a wholly owned subsidiary of the South Korean conglomerate Samsung Electronics Co., Ltd.
The campus employs between 1,000 and 4,999 people, though the company does not disclose cleanroom square footage or annual wafer volumes.

The facility supplies memory components for Samsung's own Galaxy smartphone line and SSD products, while its foundry services address custom logic and memory needs for fabless semiconductor companies and other electronics OEMs.

Samsung has positioned the Austin site as a strategic U.S. manufacturing anchor, enabling tighter supply-chain control for its memory and storage product lines and providing domestic foundry capacity for North American customers.
